result.title: Read Before You Use: Improving Visual Memory Utilization in Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Multimodal memory enables long-horizon vision-language agents to preserve and retrieve past experiences. While prior research has focused on memory construction and retrieval, effectively using the provided memory remains a challenge for vision-language models (VLMs). We find that VLMs often fail to answer downstream questions even when sufficient multimodal evidence is provided. To investigate why VLMs struggle, we replace memory images with reference captions and observe substantial performance gains, suggesting difficulties in reading visual evidence directly. However, model-generated captions may omit critical information, limiting this approach in practice. These limitations motivate a closer examination of memory utilization, revealing failures in both evidence reading and downstream question answering. Building on this distinction, we propose \textbf{MemRU}, a two-stage training framework that improves evidence reading through supervised fine-tuning (Read SFT) and downstream evidence utilization through Group Relative Policy Optimization (Use GRPO). Experimental results demonstrate that our 8B model generalizes across three unseen multimodal memory systems, outperforming Qwen3-VL-32B and approaching GPT-5-mini.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断长程多模态记忆场景下 VLM 的使用失败：即使已提供充分视觉证据仍答不对，并用参考 caption 替换记忆图像验证模型「读不懂」视觉证据；据此提出 MemRU 两阶段训练，以 Read SFT 改善证据读取、以 Use GRPO 强化下游证据利用。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接关联视觉证据筛选与「答案是否真正用到视觉内容」的问题，其图像换 caption 后显著提升的观察可供核查视觉旁路与信息坍缩；但工作聚焦记忆读取而非 latent 推理状态的生成与更新。
